title: Lower Bounds for Permuted Modular-Addition Automorphisms
summary: Quasilinear-preserving graph automorphisms can be sampled for word sizes 4 through 64, but establishing a quantitative lower bound on their number remains open.

formal_statement.body: For permuted modular addition with word size $n$, let $\mathcal{A}_n$ be the set of quasilinear-preserving graph automorphisms that are not right self-equivalences of the associated implicit function $T$. Such automorphisms can be sampled for word sizes $4 \le n \le 64$, but no lower bound on $|\mathcal{A}_n|$ has been obtained. Establish a quantitative lower bound on $|\mathcal{A}_n|$ as a function of $n$, or more generally of the input size of the permuted modular addition.

scope.domain: Algebraic study of quasilinear-preserving graph automorphisms of permuted modular addition outside the right self-equivalences of its implicit function.
parameters: Word size n, the primary size parameter for permuted modular addition
Input size of the permuted modular addition, the more general asymptotic size parameter
scope.unresolved_remainder: Establish a quantitative lower bound on the number of relevant graph automorphisms as a function of the word size or, more generally, the input size.

progress.summary: The source reports that the relevant graph automorphisms can be sampled for word sizes from 4 through 64, while no lower bound on their number was obtained. Deriving such a bound remains unresolved.
